body:
Build a throwaway state/ref protocol harness, not the production engine, to test recovery.

- [ ] Kill at registration, change-ref creation, queue persistence, candidate build, before/after trunk CAS, note write and terminal-state write.
- [ ] Restart/retry proves no acknowledged commit lost, no duplicate landing and eventual one terminal outcome for every change after sufficient recovery runs.
- [ ] Reconcile by verified trunk ancestry plus exact submitted identity; a same Change-Id on an unrelated or earlier generation is insufficient.
- [ ] Exercise duplicate/stale engine locks, lost reply, dependent rejection/requeue, incomplete notes, retained draft objects and confirmed-culprit revert crash windows.
- [ ] Commit throwaway scripts/report; failures require ADR changes before M1. Process-kill results do not establish power-loss durability.

## Objects, priority and bounded recovery

Inject crashes around manifest notes/index writes, grant/revoke/expiry, grace transfer, sev attempt preemption and persisted fix-window/full-confirmation/revert races. Prove no duplicate landing/compensation or reset deadline and no invented manifest/pass.
title: S7: Qualify receive and landing crash windows
